$about: Expected facts for the mck-chart skill's hand-run eval cases. The CSVs are synthetic and deliberately differ from the sample data the skill ships (assets/data/), so a headline cannot be copied from a cookbook example. python/tests/test_eval_cases.py recomputes the numbers from the CSVs, so these stay honest.

time_to_fill_by_job_family.prompt: Which job families are slowest to fill, and how far over the 45-day target are they?
time_to_fill_by_job_family.chart_family: sorted horizontal bar with a labelled target line (cookbook/bar.md); acceptable alternative: diverging bars of days over target (orange on the over-target side, grey on the other)
time_to_fill_by_job_family.focus_note: the two slowest; at most 2 highlighted. Blue focus on grey context, or orange for the over-target side in the diverging form (over target = worse). Never green for under target without a ▲▼ or word.
time_to_fill_by_job_family.headline_example: Six of eight job families miss the 45-day fill target, and Cybersecurity Analyst roles take twice as long at 92 days
time_to_fill_by_job_family.subtitle_example: Median days to fill by job family, period not given (days)
time_to_fill_by_job_family.suppression: none: open requisitions are not people counts, and every family has 25 or more
time_to_fill_by_job_family.source_expected: Source: [confirm source and as-of date]; 985 open requisitions across 8 job families (no system, date or period was given)
fails_if: every bar has its own color
a system name or period is invented
orange is used for the fastest families

engagement_by_site.prompt: Which sites fall short of the enterprise engagement score?
engagement_by_site.question_type: magnitude / deviation from a benchmark, values clustered far from zero
engagement_by_site.chart_family: dot plot with the enterprise rate as a labelled line (cookbook/dot-plot-dumbbell.md), or diverging bars of the gap in points; NOT a truncated bar chart (values run 64-78)
engagement_by_site.focus_note: the two sites below the 72% enterprise rate; orange is allowed because below the benchmark is worse, blue focus is fine too
engagement_by_site.headline_example: Two sites fall 6 to 8 points short of the 72% enterprise engagement score
engagement_by_site.suppression: Boise Clinic Support has 8 respondents: it must not appear in marks, labels, tooltips or the headline (merge into Other or drop), and a footnote must say one site under 10 respondents is not shown
engagement_by_site.source_expected: Source: [confirm source and as-of date]; 1,650 respondents across 7 sites shown
fails_if: Boise appears anywhere, including as the lowest site at 50%

internal_fill_two_periods.prompt: How did internal fill change from FY25 to FY26 across business units?
internal_fill_two_periods.question_type: change over time between two periods
internal_fill_two_periods.chart_family: slope chart (cookbook/slope-bump.md) or dumbbell (cookbook/dot-plot-dumbbell.md); NOT a multi-period line (only two periods) and NOT grouped bars as the first choice
internal_fill_two_periods.focus_note: the biggest fall (orange, worse) and the biggest rise (blue); at most 2 highlighted, the rest grey
internal_fill_two_periods.headline_example: Internal fill fell 8 points in Enterprise Technology while Medical-Surgical gained 8, FY25 to FY26
internal_fill_two_periods.subtitle_example: Internal fill rate by business unit, FY25 vs. FY26 (% of hires filled internally)
internal_fill_two_periods.suppression: none: the smallest group is 142 hires
internal_fill_two_periods.derived_measure_note: if the chart or headline counts internal hires (hires × rate), it must call them estimates in the footnote
internal_fill_two_periods.source_expected: Source: [confirm source and as-of date]; 3,495 hires across 6 business units, FY25-FY26
fails_if: a line chart with two points per series
the headline numbers do not match the CSV
green used for the rise without ▲ or a word
